One part is that we are trying for automization. There is a requirement for system automation. And we are working on it. There are already 2 -3 software companies with whom we are talking about Suyog Telematics Limited Q4 & FY25 Post Earnings Conference

items.statement: Management acknowledges communication gaps with investors and will rectify immediately
items.quote: I would accept that there are some communication gaps which are happening when we are declaring some results or something which we are working on and it will be rectified immediately with immediate effect and next quarter onwards, I don't see there will be any gap between investors' perception and the company's performance.

items.statement: 5,07,720 ESOPs exercised; 10-14 lakh more pending
items.quote: 5,07,720 ESOPs are taken in exercise or next 10 .14 lakhs, more pending.

items.statement: Promoter increased stake by 5% already; further investment after warrant conversion
items.quote: Sir, out of that INR521 I have already increased my 5% stake. Okay. Second part is that your suggestion is welcome No doubt at all for that I am ready to invest but the purpose is that the money will not come to the company.

items.statement: Promoters 100% ready to invest more; waiting for current warrant conversion to complete
items.quote: Promoter is 100% interested in increasing more stake. They are already -- we did warrants last time. Unless that warrant gets completed one more warrant cannot happen. So that warrant is still due for conversion right now and he is 100% ready to invest and we also got some feedback from other investors stating if only promoter invests then there can be logic that companies giving warrants to promo

items.statement: INR70 crores received since March 31; INR30 crores pipeline for Q1; total INR100 crores raised in Q1
items.quote: From 31 March till now we hav e got more or less INR70 crores. And another INR30 crore are pipeline. It will come any time in Q1. So Q1 we have already raised, you can assume that we have raised INR100 crore in Q1

items.statement: CFO Himanshu Jindal resigned; he confirmed his departure on the call and said it was a personal choice unrelated to company performance.
items.quote: Himanshu Jindal: Himanshu this side. See, I'm -- whatever is happening on my side is a very different story. So I don't think anyone should correlate with me going versus what how OBL is doing.

items.statement: QIP of around Rs. 25 crore was attempted but could not be completed due to market fall and exchange permission delays; may consider again in similar range depending on market scenario
items.quote: The last what we were expecting to raise, around Rs. 25 crore from QIP.

items.statement: Equity raising planned in 3 to 6 months timeline for debt repayment and business expansion
items.quote: now we will have some equity raising, but that will take around 3 to 6 months timeline.

items.statement: Raised Rs 10.2 crore via preferential allotment of 7.6 lakh shares at Rs 131 each, subscribed by promoters and Saint Capital Fund, Mauritius
items.quote: In the fourth quarter we raised Rs. 10.2 crores through preferential allotment. We issued 7.6 lakh equity shares at Rs. 131 each. These were subscribed mainly by the promoters and Saint Capital Fund, Mauritius.

items.statement: Consolidated cash at end of FY25 was ₹1,156 million and net cash was ₹483 million after debt
items.quote: The consolidated cash at the end of the year was ₹1,156 million, and the net cash was ₹483 million after considering outstanding debt.

items.statement: Company maintains INR100 crore liquidity buffer throughout FY25
items.quote: Additionally, we have consistently maintained a healthy liquidity buffer of approximately INR100 crores at all times during the year, reinforcing our financial resilience and operational readiness.

items.statement: Bank balance of INR111 crores held at year-end for 1.5 months business development
items.quote: Yes. So, we always keep a high liquidity at least for 1.5 month's business development amount in hand.

items.statement: Operating cash flow was negative INR 12 crores in FY25 due to unbilled revenue; management expects improvement to INR 4-5 crores in upcoming months
items.quote: As you know, currently our operating cash flow is around INR 12 crores negative and the primary reason for this is booking of the unbilled revenue which has not yet been converted into actual cash.

items.statement: Working capital cycle is 85-90 days; smart meter business expected at 45-60 days
items.quote: Sir, currently, our working capital cycle or debtor cycle is at aroun d 85 days right now, 85 to 90 days approximately on a gross sale level basis. And for smart meter, I expec t this to be around 45 to 60 days

items.statement: Full year smart meter expenses incurred were INR8-10 crores
items.quote: In the full year, I can tell you, I think we have incurred approxima tely around INR8 crores to INR10 crores

items.statement: Company raised Rs 55 crore and spent approximately Rs 10 crore on capital expenditures so far
items.quote: The Company has begun making new investments, which are taking shape. So far, out of Rs. 55 crores raised, approximately Rs. 10 crores have been spent on capital expenditures.

items.statement: FY25 capex of INR78.67 crore fully funded through internal accruals
items.quote: During the financial year 2025, the company made consolidated investments of INR78.67 crores in fixed assets on a cash basis. I'm pleased to share that this entire investment was funded entirely through internal accruals, reflecting on our strong operational cash flows and disciplined capital allocation strategy.

items.statement: Operating cash flow was Rs999 million in FY25, with net cash balance of Rs1,036 million at year end
items.quote: We continued our focus on improving the working capital metrics which resulted in solid operating cash flows at Rs999m and end the year with a net cash balance of Rs1036 million.

items.statement: Trade receivables increased by Rs152 million to Rs2,753 million in Q4 FY25 despite Rs571 million incremental sales
items.quote: Trade Receivables were at Rs2,753m during Q4FY25 vs Rs2,601m during Q4FY24. This is only a Rs152m increase in receiv ables in spite of achieving incremental sales of Rs571m over last

items.statement: Inventory decreased to Rs1,401 million in Q4 FY25 from Rs1,761 million in Q4 FY24, driven by lower raw material paper inventory
items.quote: Inventory decreased to Rs1,401m (vs Q4FY24: Rs1,761m). This inventory decrease is driven by a lower raw material paper inventory of Rs270m (vs Q4FY 24: Rs633m

items.statement: Net working capital days reduced to 151 days in Q4 FY25 from 157 days in Q4 FY24, lowest in company history
items.quote: Net W orking Capital reduced to 151 days (vs. 157 days in Q4FY24). This is the lo west Q4 net working capital days in the company’s history

items.statement: No fresh equity issuance or dilution mentioned; growth guidance excludes acquisitions
items.quote: No, that is without acquisition.

items.statement: Operating cash flow improved in Q3 and Q4 FY25 due to better receivables collection and understanding of bank spend-based patterns
items.quote: But I think the entire sales team in the last Q3 and Q4 have really done a good job in terms of one, of course, the receivables.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents including investments in securities increased to INR 148 crores in FY25 from INR 101 crores in FY24
items.quote: And cash and cash equivalents, including investments in securities for FY '25 was at INR 148 crores up from INR 101 crores in FY '24.

items.statement: New CFO Shekhar Sood appointed with two decades of global financial leadership experience across listed entities and multinationals
items.quote: Before I begin, I would like to take the pleasure to introduce you to our new CFO, Shekhar Sood. Shekhar brings in two decades of global financial leadership experience across listed entities, multinationals and high-growth companies.

items.statement: Loan to related party expected to be repaid during the year, either fully or in parts.
items.quote: I guess that loan will come back, but that we will figure out how quickly, because that loan is earning interest, and we are anyway sitting on surplus cash on this balance sheet. So that loan, sometime during this year we should expect for it to come back, if not full, then in parts.

items.statement: Working capital borrowings increased due to additional inventory buildup from imported raw materials and bulk shipments
items.quote: So basically it's not the any long term or those kind of borrowings that have increased the overall scen ario. It's basically the working capital because of the additional inventory that we are trying to build in the organization

items.statement: Cash accruals of 979 lakh from consolidated balance sheets; borrowing strategy calculated for CapEx and working capital
items.quote: Ideally, if we see our cash flows, it doesn't mean that we have our cash and we spend it overall in a CapEx and everything. So if you go through our budgets, you will see that there is 979 lakh which is the cash accruals (Net proceeds of long term borrowing) from my consolidated balance sheets.

items.statement: Cash generated from operations was Rs. 59 crores positive, mainly used to reduce debt; net cash surplus including investments is Rs. 24 crores.
items.quote: Cash generated from operations stands at Rs. 59 crores positive, which has been majorly utilized in reducing our debt. Our net cash surplus, including investment, is amounting to Rs. 24 crores.

items.statement: Promoter shareholding percentage decreased due to preferential issue in September; number of promoter shares hardly changed
items.quote: So sorry, the promoter share percentage has decreased because of one is because of the addition of the preferential issue that we did in the month of September. So if you look at really the number of shares that the promoters have, there's hardly any change.

items.statement: Preferential issue done in September 2024 caused promoter shareholding percentage to decrease
items.quote: So sorry, the promoter share percentage has decreased because of one is because of the addition of the preferential issue that we did in the month of September.

items.statement: Trade receivables increased due to INR150+ crore work done in Q4; average receivable cycle 90-120 days, currently recovering INR50-60 crore from March outstandings
items.quote: And out of that also if I have to really tell you, in Q3 and Q4 if I have to compare, the 70% of the H2 turnover has come from Q4. And that is the only reason that you would also see the increase in the trade receivables, one of the major reasons for that because almost INR150 plus crores of work have been done in Q4.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle averages 90-100 days going forward
items.quote: So approximately, see -- it will, as we see that it will -- you know, if we really look at the closing numbers, it will keep varying. But by and large, our cash conversion cycle is about, averagely 90 days. 90 to 100 days is the general cash conversion cycle.

items.statement: Merger announced between Markolines Infra (transferor) and Markolines Pavement (transferee); Markolines Infra FY25 revenue INR133 crore, PAT INR12.29 crore; merger valued at INR263 crore
items.quote: As far as the tentative, why tentative I can give, the numbers of the Markolines Infra, we did a revenue of about INR133 crores there with a bottom line of INR12.29 crore as PAT

items.statement: Operating cash flow for FY25 was INR19.23 crores
items.quote: Our cash flow from operating activities stood at INR19.23 crores.

items.statement: Cash and investments on books are roughly INR136 crores
items.quote: Currently, we have cash and investments of roughly INR136 crores on the book.

items.statement: Promoter acquired shares worth roughly INR3 crores post-IPO
items.quote: Post IPO, I have also done a further acquisition of shares for roughly INR3 crores and that basically demonstrates my personal confidence in the company and its future growth trajectory.

items.statement: Total collections for FY25 were INR545 crores, an 8% year-on-year increase
items.quote: Total collections for the year stood at INR545 crores, which is an 8% year-on-year increase.

items.statement: Company has 1 lakh shares remaining to grant under existing 2018 ESOP plan; dilution occurs on exercise over 3-4 year vesting period
items.quote: We are still left with around 1 lakh shares to be granted. Post that the company will again come up with some other, with the next plan, then we will have some impact on dilution and all. Dilution is on exercise basically, so as the employees exercise that time, we will have dilution.

items.statement: ESOP expense for FY25 was Rs 51 lakhs; FY26 expense depends on actuarial valuation based on market price
items.quote: the calculation of ESOP is based on the actua rial valuation. So actuary value when they give us, yearly, we get a valuation report from the actuary. They check the current market price and accordingly, they do a calculation and send it to us

items.statement: Deferred tax reversal of Rs 2 crores remaining on balance sheet; utilization timing depends on auditor assessment and full-year visibility
items.quote: So still we have some deferred tax in the asset which is around Rs. 2 crores or so. So in the next year, when it will be utilized that time it will be reversed.

items.statement: Company has sufficient net owned funds for RBI requirements; capital needs met through internal accruals and banking limits
items.quote: We have capital, we also have borrowed, we have banking limits through which we drive our business because capital requirements are always there in our business, the higher we grow we will have requirements.

items.statement: Pune JV plant is ready and commercial production will start shortly with validation batches expected to complete within 10 days.
items.quote: The Pune facility is now operational and commercial production will start shortly. Validation batches are underway and are expected to be completed within the next days 10 days.

items.statement: Pune JV order book covers next 90 days and first year capacity utilization expected at 60-65%.
items.quote: First year, we'll be doing around 60% to 65% of the capacity utilization, and that is very well on track. And in the beginning, we have told that the order books are also in place for first 90 days.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved in FY25 and will continue on an improving trend.
items.quote: So, we have improved a bit on our working capital cycle, if you see the numbers. And going forward also, we will be on an improving trend only.

items.statement: Cash profit of around Rs. 25 crores plus in current financial year
items.quote: You can see that in current financial year, we have very good cash flows with us, in fact around Rs. 25 crores plus cash profit is there in the books.

items.statement: Debtor days expected to reduce by 5 to 10 days due to advance payment arrangements with distributors
items.quote: We expect 5 to 10 days of debtor days should come down going forward.

items.statement: Creditor days have come down to 45 days due to MSME payment regulations
items.quote: But creditors basically have come down because of MSME. There we have to make the payments in 45 days to our creditors.

items.statement: Company holds around INR290 crores in investments as of now
items.quote: Around INR290 crores as of now.

items.statement: Repaid debt of 1,340 million during FY25, maintaining a healthy balance sheet.
items.quote: Financially, we continue to strengthen our position by repaying debt of 1,340 million during Financial Year 25, maintaining a healthy balance sheet.

items.statement: Company maintains debt-free balance sheet with cash reserve of approximately ₹29 crore
items.quote: Despite these challenges, I am proud to emphasize that we maintain a robust financial position with a debt -free balance sheet and a cash reserve of approximately ₹29 crore.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR75 crores as at March 2025
items.quote: Our liquidity position remains strong with net cash of INR75 crores as at March 2025.

items.statement: Cash balance at end of FY25 is INR80 crores
items.quote: Cash balance, we have about INR80 crores of cash balance.

items.statement: Operating cash flow was INR 166 crores for FY25
items.quote: For the year gone by, the company has generated an operating cash flow of INR 166 crores this year.

items.statement: Operating cash flow improved to Rs.192 crore in FY25, a 40% increase from prior year
items.quote: This year we improved our operating cash flow position to Rs. 192 crore, which is 40% improvement from last year.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations improved drastically from Rs.35 crore in FY24 to Rs.228 crore in FY25
items.quote: Cash flow from operations saw a drastic improvement from Rs.35 crores in FY'24 to Rs.228, crores in FY'25.

items.statement: Inventory reduced by Rs.185 crore (19% YoY) and working capital reduced by Rs.146 crore (54% YoY) in FY25
items.quote: We have reduced our inventory position by Rs.185 crore and improvement of 19% year-on-year and reduced our working capital by Rs.146 crore, which is a 54% year-on-year improvement.

items.statement: Short-term borrowing reduced from Rs.670 crore to Rs.453 crore due to improved operating cash flow
items.quote: This led to a reduction of our short term borrowing from Rs.670 crores to Rs.453 crores.

items.statement: Expect further 20% reduction in inventory and continued cash flow improvement in FY26
items.quote: Even presently, what you see still we feel there's a lot of scope, a good 20% or so reduction. What we feel should happen throughout this year.

items.statement: Received 25% (Rs.35 crore) of QIP/warrant commitment; balance 75% pending due to market conditions
items.quote: Yes, Sanjay so we had got a couple, we have got commitment for Rs.150 crores for the overall QIP and the 25% of which was Rs.35 crores we received it fully.

items.statement: Hopeful to raise remaining 75% of QIP/warrant money in FY26 when market improves
items.quote: Yes, we should be hopeful to raise it this year.

items.statement: FY25 retail operating cash flow was Rs 44 crores
items.quote: Because if I look at your FY '25 operating cash flow in the retail business, it's closer to Rs. 44 odd crores, right

items.statement: Inventory increased due to raw material procurement for second production line not yet in commercial production
items.quote: Our inventory is high just because of the inventory which we have procured to operate the second production line and which is not reflected into numbers and which was not billed to the client.

items.statement: Higher debtors due to strong March sales of INR135 crores with recovery in April-May
items.quote: Similarly, for debtors in the month of March, our turnover was INR135 crores and a lot of EPC has also contributed to it. And there are some debtors which we are recovering in the current April and May month.

items.statement: Standalone EPC debtors INR69.21 crores, module debtors INR42.03 crores, total INR111.24 crores as of 31 March 2025
items.quote: On the standalone basis, the EPC debtors are INR69 crores and INR69.21 crores and the module is INR42.03 crores. So, the total is INR111.24 crores.

items.statement: Customer advances of INR58 crores as of 31 March 2025
items.quote: And with regards to the advance from customers, it is INR58 crores of advance, what we have on 31 March '25.

items.statement: No equity raise planned for 2.2 GW expansion, funded through internal accruals and previous preferential allotment
items.quote: The current expansion is being supported through the internal accruals. So fortunately, we have very good cash accruals. So for this 2.2 gigawatt, we are not raising any equity.

items.statement: Planning INR500 crores equity raise for cell and module expansion within 2-3 months
items.quote: We are approaching investors to raise. So I think so within 2 to 3 months, we will be approaching investors to raise this INR500 crores.
